title: Acceptability and effectiveness of different information letters for recruiting patients in hospitals
summary: As part of a cross-sectional study on patients' sleep in hospitals (Sleep Acute), an embedded cluster-randomised controlled study comparing two written study information forms is conducted. While the first group receives a formal information letter, patients in the second group are given an information leaflet including a link to an information video. In a random and representative selection of 30 hospitals in Cologne and catchment area 1,000 patients from 100 selected general wards will be included. Primary efficacy endpoint is the proportion of people participating in the cross-sectional study in both groups. Acceptability will be assessed by means of a questionnaire.

interventions.name: Receipt of a formal information letter on the day of data collection during hospital stay
Receipt of an information leaflet on the day of data collection during hospital stay

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Hospitals:
general hospitals (inpatient units), hospitals providing at least basic care (internal medicine and surgery), hospitals within 50km of the study centre

Wards:
bed-managing wards, general wards

Patients:
age ≥ 18 years, capacity to consent, stay of ≥ 2 nights, informed consent for study participation
Exclusion criteria:
Hospitals:
Other hospitals (exclusively psychiatric or neurological beds, exclusively day-care patients), armed forces hospitals, preventive care and rehabilitation facilities

Wards:
palliative care units, psychiatric wards, paediatric wards, emergency departments, functional units, intermediate and intensive care units 

Patients:
Cognitive and/or physical impairments that do not allow the completion of the questionnaire, insufficient knowledge of the German language that does not allow the completion of the questionnaire
